claim_verdicts.evidence: Test/service/controller parts verified at stage-1: two cancel tests (OrderServiceTests.cs:46,58); CancelOrderAsync (OrderService.cs:29-38) never reads Status and calls notifier.Send; Cancel (OrdersController.cs:42-46) returns Ok(ToDto(order)). But there is no separate cancellation change in history: git log stage-1 on the three files shows only 610e283 (whole backend) and 4fca60a (List()). "constructor unchanged" has no diff to compare against. FakeOrderRepository.Seed (FakeOrderRepository.cs:28) exists only for the cancel test.
claim_verdicts.source: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: OrderServiceTests.cs:45-63; OrderService.cs:29-38; OrdersController.cs:12,40-46; FakeOrderRepository.cs:28; git log stage-1 -- <files>
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Last, the controller. `OrdersController.Cancel` takes the id, calls `orderService.CancelOrderAsync(id)` and returns the order as a DTO, so it passes the layers check. It uses the `OrderService` the constructor already receives for `Create`, so there is nothing new for the dependencies check.

claim_verdicts.evidence: review-comments-examples.md@stage-1 l.3: "Các nhận xét dưới đây đều lấy từ pull request thêm chức năng hủy đơn." First comment under "Nhận xét tốt" (l.7-9): "**Bắt buộc sửa.** Ở `OrderService.Cancel`, đơn `shipped` cũng bị chuyển sang `cancelled`. ... Bạn thêm một điều kiện, hay mình hiểu sai tiêu chí?" - ends with a question.
story-example.md@stage-1 l.5-6: "Là **khách hàng**, tôi muốn **hủy đơn hàng chưa thanh toán của mình**". AC3: "Khi đơn ở trạng thái `paid`, `shipped` hoặc `cancelled`, nút \"Hủy đơn\" không hiện."

Factual part (tool shows files by path) supported by execution: `git show 4fca60a --stat` in examples/don-hang lists DonHang.Api/..., DonHang.Domain/..., DonHang.Infrastructure/..., DonHang.Tests/FakeOrderRepository.cs last - path order, tests at the end. git-diff docs: -O<orderfile> "Control the order in which files appear in the output"; unmatched paths keep "the normal order". Reading-order part is the outline's method (opinion, hedged "reads better").

No official doc governs it. Nearest repo support: review-comments-examples.md table row: "\"OK.\" trên một PR 800 dòng | Duyệt mà không đọc; tệ hơn là không duyệt." That supports "a bare approval of a large PR can mean it was not read", not a frequency ("usually"). Outline item 3 uses "usually", so the wording is outline-sanctioned but unsupported as a generalisation.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: A 300-line PR approved after fifteen minutes with no comments is a warning sign: the team's own review examples call a bare "OK." on a large PR approving without reading.

issues.text: Unlisted claim, stated as fact: that one complete review gives the author a clearer picture than comments sent one at a time. No source in the repo docs or versions.yaml supports it, and it is not in the outline.
issues.quote: the author gets a clearer picture from one complete review than from comments arriving one at a time
issues.fix: Either drop the comparison ("Finish it, then send all comments together. One found problem does not mean it is the only one.") or add the sentence to claims as kind opinion, section 7, and soften to "many authors find one complete review easier to act on".

issues.text: Option c is marked wrong but is literally true of the real file: OrderService.cs@stage-1 lines 25-28 carry the comment "Deliberately missing a check: an order already `shipped` still gets cancelled here." Try it tells the learner to open that file, so a learner who did Try it can defend c. The explanation hedges to "the lesson's quoted service code", which the stem does not say.
issues.quote: The second file has a comment naming the bug
issues.fix: Replace option c with a clearly false distractor, e.g. en "The service logs an error for `shipped` orders" / vi "Service ghi log lỗi với đơn `shipped`", explanation "CancelOrderAsync logs nothing; it sets the status and sends a notification."

issues.text: Presents "the cancellation change at stage-1" as a real change touching three places and says the controller's constructor is "unchanged". No such diff exists (cancellation arrived in 610e283 with the whole backend), and FakeOrderRepository.Seed is a fourth place added only for the cancel test.
issues.quote: The cancellation change at stage-1 touches three places: a test file, the service and the controller.
issues.fix: Write: "At stage-1 the cancellation code lives mainly in three files: a test file, the service and the controller." Replace the constructor sentence with claim 1's suggested_text.

issues.text: Text in a code span is presented as the file's wording but differs: the source has backticks around shipped and cancelled and a line break ("đơn `shipped` cũng bị chuyển sang / `cancelled`").
issues.quote: `đơn shipped cũng bị chuyển sang cancelled`
issues.fix: Quote it as plain text in quotation marks, not a code span, or say "says, in Vietnamese, that a `shipped` order also gets moved to `cancelled`".

issues.text: Expected result for step 2 says "any of" but omits a valid answer: CancelOrderAsync also cancels a `paid` order, which AC3 of story-example.md forbids and no test covers. A learner who writes that is not matched by the key.
issues.quote: any of: it sends a notification on cancel; it cancels a `shipped` order; it cancels an order that is already `cancelled`
issues.fix: Write: "any of: it sends a notification on cancel; it cancels a `paid` or `shipped` order; it cancels an order that is already `cancelled`."

issues.text: Try it has the learner open OrderService.cs at stage-1, whose comment (l.27) says "`DonHang.Tests` covers `new`/`paid` but not `shipped`". False: no test seeds `paid` (OrderServiceTests.cs:45-63). This contradicts the lesson's own correct step-1 answer and will confuse the learner.
issues.fix: Propose a repo change via prompt 08: OrderService.cs line 27 -> "`DonHang.Tests` covers `new` and an unknown id but not `shipped`". No lesson text change needed if lines 29-38 stay byte-identical.

issues.text: Frequency claim ("usually") with no evidence; see claim 5 verdict. Repeated in summary line 5.
issues.quote: A 300-line PR approved after fifteen minutes with no comments usually means the reviewer skimmed it, not that there was nothing to say.
issues.fix: Use claim 5 suggested_text; soften summary line 5 the same way ("...is a warning sign that it was skimmed").

issues.text: Unconditioned generalisation about authors, not in claims. Nearest support is the repo doc's "Nhiều nhận xét không có nghĩa là bạn làm tệ. Nó có nghĩa là có người đọc kỹ."
issues.fix: Replace with: "the team's own guide for authors says many comments mean someone read carefully, not that the author did badly." Add to claims (fact, source review-comments-examples.md, section "Khi bạn là tác giả").

issues.text: 'the build is green' is not in known_vocab and not defined. From the reviewing-for-tests summary I know 'the build' can catch a gap, but I have to guess that 'green' means every test passed. Quiz q4 ('all had green builds') and q5 option d depend on the same phrase.
issues.fix: Write 'the build is green (it compiles and every test passes)' at its first use in section 2.
issues.quote: Nothing looked wrong, the build is green, and you are about to write "looks good" and approve.

The only hint that statuses go new, paid, shipped comes later, in the Try it expected result.
issues.fix: Name the story file (`docs/team/story-example.md`) and add one clause after 'unpaid orders' saying that a `shipped` order has already been paid, so the story does not cover it.
issues.quote: The story behind this work is about unpaid orders, so the first question writes itself: what happens to an order that has already shipped?
